Hardwick in the U.S., which was later overturned), courts argued that if the right to privacy protected sodomy, it could logically extend to protect other acts that society deems harmful, such as incest, adultery, or polygamy.   • Quality of Life: Some proponents suggest that the open proliferation of sexual "libertinism" degrades the moral environment of a community. They argue that laws against sodomy help maintain a public atmosphere that is conducive to raising children and fostering civic virtue.

In short, supporters of reinstating laws against sodomy and non-procreative sex do not view these laws as arbitrary discrimination, but rather as essential instruments for maintaining moral order, protecting public health, preserving the traditional family, and upholding the right of communities to legislate based on collective moral standards.
